To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the erythrogram and ferritin have a low accuracy for the diagnosis of anemia in pregnancy and the responsiveness to the oral iron-therapy is a good predictor for the functional iron-deficiency.

the erythrogram and the serum ferritin are not accurate tests for diagnosis of functional iron deficiency in pregnancy, and the cutoff point of serum ferritin for diagnosis of functional anemia should be 15 μg/L. This
serum ferritin has the best performance to predict the therapeutic responsiveness to iron therapy in pregnancy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a diagnostic study on the prediction of the iron-therapy response in anemia of pregnancy.
the diagnostic accuracy of the serum ferritin and of some erythrogram parameters for the diagnosis of iron-deficiency in the pregnancy.
the accuracy of the erythrocyte parameters and serum ferritin to predict the therapeutic response to iron therapy in anemic pregnant women.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study is a diagnostic accuracy study that aims to verify the accuracy and cutoff points of serum ferritin (SF) and erythrogram for diagnosis of functional iron deficiency in pregnancy using the responsiveness to oral iron as gold-standard.
the serum ferritin and the red cell distribution width are the best tests to diagnose iron-deficiency in anemic pregnant women, and the red cell count and haematocrit are not recommended.
the study is a phase III diagnostic accuracy study to evaluate erythrogram and the serum ferritin for maternal anemia diagnosis in pregnancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the accuracy of erythrogram is low for the maternal anemic diagnosis, and serum ferrtin is the best test for the diagnosis of iron deficiency in pregnancy.
the serum ferritin and the haemoglobin are not accurate tests to guide the iron-therapy in pregnancy.
the study is registered in the WHO-ICTRP.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of the serum ferritin concentration in the diagnosis of functional anemia in pregnancy could be more accurate than the haemoglobin level, which is the most used parameter for the diagnosis of iron-deficiency in this population.

serum ferritin is a more reliable predictor of iron deficiency than hemoglobin, and that the cutoff point of 15 ng/mL for serum ferritin is more accurate for the diagnosis of iron deficiency in pregnancy than 12 ng/mL, the most commonly accepted cutoff point.

the use of serum ferritin is not enough to diagnose iron-deficiency anemiain pregnancy, and the use of erythrogram could be useful for this aim, since the mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration and the reticulocyte counts were the best tests to discriminate iron-deficiency anemic pregnant women from the non-iron-deficient anemic ones.
